commands.review_summary:
The PR changes the Codex app-server event projector to fail closed on explicit unknown item statuses, warn once on unknown or mismatched notifications, and adds focused regression tests.

PR surface: Source +63, Tests +290. Total +353 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. source-reproducible: current main maps an explicit unrecognized Codex item status to completed and drops current-turn unknown notification methods without warning. I did not execute tests in this read-only review.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] Needs contributor real-behavior proof and maintainer acceptance of the compatibility tradeoff before merge; the code finding is narrow but does not by itself clear the proof gate.

target.title: fix(codex): fail-closed on unknown item statuses and warn on dropped notifications
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Codex event projector **failed open** on protocol drift: unrecognized item statuses were mapped to `"completed"` (so a tool that actually failed or carried an unknown status was projected as **success**), and unknown notification methods plus thread/turn correlation mismatches were **silently dropped** with no breadcrumb — converting future Codex protocol drift into wrong results instead of diagnosable errors.

Closes #99269.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three fail-open / silent-drop sites in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.ts`:

1. **`itemStatus` fail-open** — the trailing fallthrough returned `"completed"` for every unrecognized status. Now fail-closes to `"failed"` (mirroring the file's own `auditNativeToolTerminalStatus`, which already refuses to assume success for ambiguous statuses). Known mappings (`failed`/`error`→failed, `declined`→blocked, `inProgress`/`in_progress`/`running`→running, `completed`/missing→completed) are **unchanged**.
2. **Unknown notification method** — the `handleNotification` `default:` case dropped unknown methods silently. Now warns once per method (behavior unchanged — still dropped).
3. **Thread/turn correlation mismatch** — the early `return;`s dropped mismatched notifications silently. Now warns once per `method+thread+turn` (behavior unchanged). `turn/completed` is guarded: a `turn/completed` for a non-active turn is dropped by the turn-router before reaching the projector, so a correlation warning there would be unreachable.

Warn-once dedup uses `Set`s keyed per `item-type+status`, per `method`, and per `method+thread+turn` — rate-limited diagnostics at the projector boundary, as the issue asks. The item-status `Set` is module-level (process-lifetime rate-limiting for a bounded status set); the notification `Set`s are per-projector-instance.

## Codex protocol verification (hard gate)

Per the repo's Codex gate, I personally inspected `openai/codex` (`codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/v2/`) for the item-status values Codex actually emits:

- `CommandExecutionStatus.ts` → `inProgress | completed | failed | declined`
- `PatchApplyStatus.ts` (fileChange) → `inProgress | completed | failed | declined`
- `McpToolCallStatus.ts`, `DynamicToolCallStatus.ts`, `CollabAgentToolCallStatus.ts` → `inProgress | completed | failed`
- `ImageGenerationItem.status` (free-form `String` in `ext/items/src/image_generation.rs`); the only emitter (`ext/image-generation/src/tool.rs`) sets `in_progress` / `failed` / `completed`.
- `TurnStatus.ts` → `completed | failed | inProgress | interrupted` — `interrupted` applies to **turns**, not items routed through `itemStatus`.

Every item-status literal Codex emits is already in the projector's known set, so the fail-closed path only catches genuinely-unknown/future strings. No status was added; `pausedByProtocol` / `queued` / `cancelled` / `needs_permission` / `unresolved` are **not** real Codex item statuses.

## User Impact

When Codex introduces a new item status (protocol drift), the projector no longer silently treats it as success — the tool result is marked `failed`/`isError` and a single rate-limited warning names the unrecognized status. Unknown notification methods and correlation mismatches now leave a breadcrumb instead of vanishing, making drift diagnosable. Behavior for all known statuses and for dropped notifications is otherwise unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused vitest (local, Node 24):
- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` — **131 passed** (5→6 new tests added: unknown status→`failed`+`isError` + warn-once-per-status; a *second* unrecognized status (`queued`) still warns, confirming per-status dedup; unknown-method warn-once + drop preserved; correlation-mismatch warn-once + drop preserved; known statuses map correctly with zero warnings; `turn/completed` mismatch emits zero warnings).
- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts -t "turn/completed"` — **2 passed | 115 skipped**, no regression. (4 unrelated `run-attempt` auth-profile/elicitation failures reproduce identically on `upstream/main` with this diff reverted — pre-existing, not caused by this change.)
- `tsgo` typecheck (`extensions/codex/tsconfig.json`): exit 0. `oxlint` on touched files: exit 0. `git diff --check`: clean.

Behavior preservation: warn calls are inserted strictly **before** the existing `return;`/`break;`/fallthrough (control flow unchanged); the test diff has **0 removed lines** (no existing assertion weakened); 125 pre-existing tests pass unmodified.

In-process real-behavior proof (vitest harness feeding `CodexAppServerEventProjector` directly — not a provider live-run):
```
scenario 1 — unknown status 'pausedByProtocol' (×2):
  item projected status = failed | isError = true ; unrecognized-status warnings = 1 (dedup)
scenario 2 — unknown method 'item/futureStatus/updated' (×2):
  unknown-method warnings = 1 (dedup) ; tool events emitted = 0 (dropped, unchanged)
scenario 3 — item/completed for turn 'turn-other' (active 'turn-1', ×2):
  correlation-mismatch warnings = 1 (dedup) ; tool events emitted = 0 (dropped, unchanged)
```

## Relation to existing PRs

- **#99754** takes the same correct fail-closed approach and is code-green, but is blocked on the contributor-proof gates this PR satisfies: it lacks the required `What Problem This Solves`/`Evidence` sections (the "Real behavior proof" gate) and a flaky QA Smoke e2e; it also does not guard `turn/completed` (a ClawSweeper noise flag).
- **#99287** has a fatal build defect (imports a never-defined `describeCodexNotificationCorrelation`) and a dirty merge.

This PR ships the evidence/proof sections, the `turn/completed` guard, regression tests (incl. per-status dedup), and a clean build.
